claims: Planning Data API exposes search entity as /entity.{extension} with json, html or geojson.
The q parameter searches by postcode or UPRN.
typology, dataset, organisation_entity, entity, curie, prefix and reference are supported filters.
period controls inclusion of current or all entries.
start-date components and a match mode support temporal filtering.
longitude requires latitude and latitude requires longitude for point-intersection search.
geometry accepts WKT and coordinates are documented as WGS84 EPSG:4326.
geometry_entity filters using geometries of supplied entity IDs.
geometry_reference filters using geometries of entities matching supplied references.
geometry_curie filters using geometries of entities matching supplied CURIEs.
geometry_relation supports within, equals, disjoint, intersects, touches, contains, covers, coveredby, overlaps and crosses.
limit controls result count and offset paginates results.
response links provide next, prev, first and last pagination URLs.
field restricts returned fields.
exclude_field removes fields unless field explicitly takes precedence.
quality is a supported entity-search filter.
Get entity returns one entity by numeric entity ID.
List datasets and Get dataset are separate endpoints.
multiple dataset parameters may be supplied in a single entity search.
coordinate searches return entities whose geometries intersect the point.
UPRN lookup is documented as more precise than coordinates for registered properties.
entity responses include dataset, name, start-date, geometry and point where available.
absence of results does not prove absence of constraints because coverage varies.
geometry WKT spaces must be percent encoded by the client.
no batch endpoint is provided for portfolio queries.
one request per property is required for API portfolio screening.
polite rate limiting is required for repeated API requests.
bulk downloads are recommended for hundreds of properties or more.
bulk processing gives a stable local snapshot and avoids API rate limits.
bulk formats include CSV and JSON.
GeoJSON is available where applicable.
Parquet is available for large datasets where provided.
dataset-page download URL formats vary by dataset.
the API is documented as beta and may change.
planning-application specification is in development and may change.
local planning authorities are not currently required to share application data to that specification.
start_date_match examples include since for recent applications.
geometry_entity can combine a target dataset with an administrative boundary entity.
field can reduce payload to name, dataset and reference for screening.
entity ID lookup is distinct from free-text q search.
reference and CURIE are first-class filters rather than inferred identifiers.
current versus historical selection must be explicit when lifecycle matters.
offset must advance consistently with limit to avoid duplicate or skipped pages.
pre-built response links are safer than hand-constructed pagination when present.
bulk and API outputs must not be assumed byte-identical without snapshot evidence.
candidate binding requires an actual candidate-specific entity response.
constructed candidate URLs alone are not authoritative readback evidence.
coverage variation requires fail-closed treatment of zero results.
exact boundary identity cannot be promoted from generic planning entity contracts.
numeric elevation cannot be promoted from Planning Data API metadata.

attempt_result: documented entity patterns and candidate URLs revalidated; execution URL safety still prevents authoritative bytes
